evidence: Swap test fails: the frame (white header with a 16px line icon and the name in bold body text, pale grey-blue ground, single left column of bold-label native inputs, dark blue-teal rectangular primary button, 'There is a problem' red error summary, grey key/value summary list, one-line footer) would carry a GP appointment booking or a council permit form unchanged; only the anchor glyph and the words change.

Category-guess test fails: the predicted default for a small public-facing booking service (government-style form pattern, one muted blue accent, white/grey ground, no imagery) is exactly what is shown on all five surfaces; nothing comes from the harbour's physical world (charts, tide boards, quay signage, pontoon layout).

Similar-prompt test fails: a brief for 'campsite pitch booking at a small coastal site' would plausibly produce the same structure, the same accent, the same card-radio list (root, berths) and the same summary list (review, confirmed).

Product-bound elements exist only as content: the tide-times table and sill-gate sentence on / (1280 y 620-1070), 'Afloat at every state of the tide' / 'Settles on soft mud at low water' on /berths.html. The tide table, the one element that could have been the signature, is styled as a default zebra-less data table with misaligned column headers.

unfinished: Browser-default controls on show: native date input reading 'yyyy/mm/dd' with the system calendar glyph and native select chevrons on / at every width.
Identity is only the name: 'Saltmarsh Quay' in bold body text beside a small stock anchor glyph; no mark, no colour or type moment of its own.
No focal point beyond the heading on any screen; every surface is a heading, a paragraph and a stack of identical 320px fields.
Sections that are only a heading and a list: 'Harbour rules' on / is an h2 and three default bullets.

Bands that stop short: on /boat.html, /review.html, /confirmed.html and the length-over-limit state the white footer band ends mid-viewport with the grey page ground continuing below it (1280: footer ends at y~800, ~475 and ~295).

Half-empty layout at wide widths: content sits in a ~540px left column inside a 850px container, leaving the right 40-60% of the 1280/1440 viewport empty, and the lone '...' menu button floats detached at the far right of /berths.html.
Headings differ from body mainly in size and weight of the same family; the tide table headers 'Morning'/'Afternoon' are left-set over right-aligned figures.
evidence: / 1280 and 375 default: the first viewport is a heading, two lines of intro, three native controls and a button on a flat pale grey ground; nothing to look at that a skipper would recognise as this harbour.
/berths.html 1280: four bordered white cards with radio circles; clean but template-like.
/confirmed.html 1280: the booking reference in bold body text inside a sentence, three key/value rows and a link, then 400px of empty grey below the footer.
Execution is orderly and readable (consistent left edge at x=208, consistent spacing, legible contrast), so it is not unappealing; it is clean but bare.
